description: How MeowDB's press-Up portals become 3D portals (docs/runtime/MAP_ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.4, docs/runtime/WORLD_RUNTIME.md). MeowDB decides which portals exist and where they lead (game/data/canonical/maps); this file holds only isometric adaptations, each with a reason. Read through WorldTuning; never duplicated in code.

force_link_mode.reason: Milestone M2 "Walkable island" (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 6): empty, so every link takes its default_link_mode or link_modes override (trail links walk through their gates, door links warp). Set to "warp" for the M1 fallback: every link press-Up only, every trail mouth plugged, trails as scenery (the L3 tour runs in both). The debug console switches links at runtime (linkmode / map_link_mode -> PortalGraph.set_link_mode).

default_link_mode.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4: trail links default to walkable edges, door links are always warps (interiors sit on the separate interior stage). Used when force_link_mode is empty (the M2 default).

link_modes.reason: Per-link overrides keyed by link id (T_<mapA>_<portalA>__<mapB>_<portalB>), each {"mode": "edge"|"warp", "reason": "...", "verified": false}. A trail the player cannot walk because of source geometry stays warp here, with the blocker recorded for the Blender pass (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.13, docs/runtime/WORLD_RUNTIME.md "Source world status"). None today: T_000001012_west00__000001014_east00 was kept warp until the Blender round-3 export (its trail climbed inside 000001012's containment band); since then 000001014 sits 12.9 m further out and the trail follows an authored 64.9 m route 3.46 m from 000001014's ring wall and 3.74 m from 000001012's, and the traversal bot walks it both ways in edge mode with no stall, recovery or invariant violation, so all 20 trails walk (docs/runtime/traversal_report.json).

destination_overrides.reason: Destination resolution rule 1 (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4): '<map_id>.<portal>' -> {"destination_portal_id" or "destination_spawn_index", "reason"}. Rule 2 (the unique reciprocal) resolves 46 of 47 MeowDB portals and rule 3 (playerSpawns[0]) the one-way 000000030.out00, so none are needed.

arrival_gates.reason: Non-canonical arrival points (portal_type 'arrival', interaction walk_only). MeowDB 000000040 has no portal back to 000000030, so the walking end of the one-way 30 -> 40 trail is an adaptation gate at Iteration One's former 40000 in00 anchor. Its spawn_transform is player_spawns[0] of 000000040, so a press-Up from 30 and a walk down the trail land identically (section 4.4). It has no press-Up trigger node: in edge mode it is the walk-through gate at the foot of the one-way ledge (GateDef into 000000040, committing 000000030.out00), in warp mode only the arrival point of the press-Up.

gates.reason: 000000030.out00 -> 000000040 is MeowDB's only one-way link (000000040 lists only east00); the trail's 40-side end needs an arrival point.

one_way_allowlist.reason: Directed links with no way back, allowed by the strongly-connected-component check (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.13 L0). Canonical: 000000040 has no portal to 000000030 on its MeowDB page.
one_way_allowlist.verification: game/data/canonical/maps/000000040.json lists only east00 (to 000000041); 000000030.out00 is the only portal into 000000040 with no reciprocal (to_portal_derivation none).

one_way_ledge.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4 CI invariant for each allowlisted one-way link (30 -> 40): jump_apex_m_at_cap + step_up_m + clearance_margin_m <= ledge height <= max_drop_m, so a player can drop down the ledge but never jump or step back up it. max_drop_m is the Blender validator one-way drop cap (AUTHORING.md, 2.6 m); the jump apex and step-up come from the player MovementModel (canonical jump table x WorldScale, data/misostory/movement.json). The ledge face must lie on the arrival gate plane (footprint + containment.ring_offset_m) within gate_plane_tolerance_m (section 4.13 L1).

hidden_portal_types.reason: MeowDB publishes the raw portal type only (2 on 46 portals, 1 on 000001020.in00, which its page lists as 'Inside portal'); it does not say type 1 is invisible. MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4 follows classic behaviour: type 1 shows no swirl and no prompt, but press-Up still works. The hedge lane is the in-world hint (open question 5).

trigger.reason: Press-Up trigger box centred on the anchor (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4): 4.5 m wide = the authored architecture-free corridor at every edge anchor (AUTHORING.md), 3 m tall = more than twice the ~1.3 m maximum jump, 1.6 m deep so the 1.5 m arrival point (plus the body radius) sits outside it.

arrival.reason: Arrivals stand 1.5 m inward of the destination anchor along the anchor normal (edges) or the door's facing (doors), facing inward (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4, graft from proposal A). That is outside the 1.6 m deep trigger, so the player never arrives inside a portal.

gates.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4 "Gates": the walk-through commit plane at each end of an edge-mode trail stands on the map ring line (footprint + containment.ring_offset_m), across the 4.5 m authored corridor (half_width_m 2.25), from below_m under the ground to height_m above it (3 m, more than twice the ~1.3 m maximum jump, so a jump across still arms it). Walking back out more than disarm_back_m behind the plane disarms it. GateMonitor treats a tick that moves the feet farther than teleport_step_m (no walk, jump or knockback covers 2 m in 1/60 s) as a teleport, never as a crossing.

anti_ping_pong.reason: The portal a player arrives at stays disarmed until the player has been outside its trigger (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4), so holding Up through an arrival never bounces back.

interaction.reason: Up (portal_enter) is MapleStory's portal key; MisoStory also lets the interact key (F) enter a portal when that portal is the nearest interactable, so a player who learned 'F talks' is not stuck (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.4).
